offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (first/second/third); Class D Felony (fourth); Class B Felony (fifth); Class A Felony (sixth+)
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While intoxicated (BAC .08 or higher)
Or while under the influence of any intoxicating liquor, drug, or controlled substance to a degree that rendered the person incapable of safely operating a vehicle
enhancements: Child passenger under 16 (§ 5-65-303, separate Class A Misdemeanor)
Fourth or subsequent offense within 5 years (felony)
notes: Arkansas uses 'DWI' rather than 'DUI.' Implied consent under § 5-65-202. Refusal results in 180-day license suspension. Lookback period is 5 years for enhancement purposes.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While intoxicated (BAC .08 or higher) or under the influence of intoxicants
No prior DWI convictions within 5 years
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours imprisonment; completion of alcohol education program; 6-month license suspension
enhancements: Refusal of chemical test (180-day license suspension)
notes: Court may order community service in lieu of minimum jail time. Restricted driving permit available after 30 days.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (second/third); Class D Felony (fourth); Class B Felony (fifth); Class A Felony (sixth+)
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While intoxicated or under the influence
One or more prior DWI convictions within 5 years
notes: Fourth DWI within 5 years is a Class D Felony. Fifth is Class B Felony. Sixth or subsequent is Class A Felony. Ignition interlock required for repeat offenders.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any controlled substance
To a degree that rendered the person incapable of safely operating a vehicle
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limit. State must prove actual impairment. Includes prescription medications. Same penalty structure as alcohol DWI.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DWI. Eight points on driving record.

statute_title: Duty to Stop — Accident Involving Death or Personal Injury
offense_class: Class D Felony (injury/death); Class C Misdemeanor (property damage under § 27-53-102)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving the scene involving death or injury is a Class D Felony. Property damage only is a Class C Misdemeanor under § 27-53-102.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Negligently caused the death of another person
The intoxication was a proximate cause of the death
notes: Charged when a DWI results in death. May also be prosecuted as manslaughter (§ 5-10-104) or negligent homicide (§ 5-10-105).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant negligently caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Arkansas does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths may be charged as negligent homicide (Class A Misdemeanor) or manslaughter (§ 5-10-104, Class C Felony) depending on culpability.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class B Misdemeanor (second); Class A Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Driving on a DWI-related suspension carries additional penalties. Third or subsequent offense within 3 years is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony (basic); Class C Felony (if creating substantial risk of injury)
elements: A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was given by hand, voice, siren, or light
Defendant willfully refused to stop
Defendant fled or attempted to elude the officer in a vehicle
enhancements: Creating a substantial risk of serious physical injury or death to another person (Class C Felony)
notes: Fleeing on foot is a separate misdemeanor offense. Vehicular fleeing is always a felony in Arkansas.

offense_class: Class D Felony (Schedule I/II); Class A Misdemeanor (Schedule III-VI)
penalty_max: 6 years (Class D Felony); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Arkansas Controlled Substances Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or park (§ 5-64-411)
notes: Arkansas reclassified simple possession in 2011. Schedule I/II substances are Class D Felony. Schedule III-VI are Class A Misdemeanor. Drug court diversion available for eligible defendants.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under 4 oz.); Class D Felony (4 oz.+)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
For personal use only (not for sale)
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession of 4 oz. or more (Class D Felony)
Possession near a school or park
notes: Arkansas passed medical marijuana via Amendment 98 in 2016. Recreational use remains illegal. Under 4 oz. for personal use is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Arkansas
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or park
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II. Any amount of possession is a Class D Felony. Larger quantities may support trafficking or delivery charges.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or park
notes: Meth is a significant problem in Arkansas. Simple possession is Class D Felony. Manufacturing carries much harsher penalties under § 5-64-423.

offense_class: Class Y Felony (most serious non-capital)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance in a quantity meeting trafficking thresholds
Specific weight thresholds vary by substance
enhancements: Trafficking near a school or park
notes: Class Y Felony is Arkansas's most serious non-capital offense. Weight thresholds: cocaine 28g, meth 28g, heroin 2g, marijuana 500 lbs. Mandatory minimum of 10 years cannot be suspended.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III/IV); Class D Felony (Schedule V/VI)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant delivered or sold a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Delivery to a minor (§ 5-64-411, enhanced one class)
Delivery near a school, park, or church (§ 5-64-411)
notes: Arkansas uses 'delivery' rather than 'distribution.' Delivery to a minor elevates the offense by one felony class.

offense_class: Class B Felony (most substances); Class C Felony (marijuana cultivation under 100 plants)
elements: Defendant manufactured, produced, or cultivated a controlled substance
Or possessed precursors with intent to manufacture
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Manufacturing near a school or park
notes: Manufacturing meth carries enhanced penalties. Arkansas Methamphetamine Cleanup Act provides for additional civil penalties and cleanup costs.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (possession); Class D Felony (delivery)
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia

With the purpose to use it to plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, process, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale, or otherwise introduce a controlled substance into the body
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Class D Felony)
notes: Possession is a Class A Misdemeanor. Delivery or sale of paraphernalia is a Class D Felony. Delivery to a minor carries additional enhancements.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III/IV); Class D Felony (Schedule V/VI)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the purpose to deliver the substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church (§ 5-64-411)
notes: Arkansas uses 'purpose to deliver' rather than 'intent to distribute.' Purpose can be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, and cash.

offense_class: Class Y Felony (Capital if aggravating factors under § 5-4-602)
penalty_min: 10 years (non-capital); life without parole or death (capital)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With the premeditated and deliberated purpose of causing the death
Or caused death in the course of committing a felony
enhancements: Felony murder (death during commission of certain felonies)
Murder of law enforcement or first responder
notes: Arkansas is a death penalty state. Capital murder requires at least one aggravating circumstance. Class Y Felony is the most serious non-capital offense.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another person under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
Or caused the death of another person while committing or attempting to commit a felony
notes: Second-degree murder covers depraved-heart killings and some felony murders that don't qualify as first-degree.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Under circumstances that would otherwise be murder
But the killing was committed under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance for which there was a reasonable excuse
notes: Arkansas's manslaughter statute covers what most states call voluntary manslaughter. The defendant must show adequate provocation or extreme emotional disturbance.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Defendant was aware of and consciously disregarded a substantial risk
notes: Covers reckless killings that don't rise to the level of extreme indifference. Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly engaged in conduct that created a substantial danger of death or serious physical injury to another person
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the value of human life
enhancements: Against law enforcement, firefighter, or teacher
notes: Arkansas distinguishes between aggravated assault (creating risk) and battery (causing actual injury). Aggravated assault on certain officials is a Class B Felony under § 5-13-211.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant purposely created apprehension of imminent physical injury in another person
Or recklessly engaged in conduct creating a substantial risk of physical injury
notes: Third-degree assault is the basic assault offense. Second-degree assault (§ 5-13-206) is a Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree); Class C Felony (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree)
elements: Defendant purposely caused serious physical injury to another person
Or caused serious physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
enhancements: Against law enforcement or certain officials
notes: Arkansas maintains separate assault (creating risk/apprehension) and battery (causing injury) statutes. Three degrees based on injury severity and mental state.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed a theft
Defendant used or threatened to use physical force upon another person
With purpose to commit the theft or to resist apprehension
notes: Base robbery is a Class B Felony. Aggravated robbery (§ 5-12-103) involving a deadly weapon or serious physical injury is a Class Y Felony.

offense_class: Class Y Felony
elements: Defendant committed a robbery
Defendant was armed with a deadly weapon or represented by word or conduct to be so armed
Or inflicted or attempted to inflict death or serious physical injury
notes: Class Y Felony — the most serious non-capital offense. No parole eligibility until 70% of sentence served.

offense_class: Class Y Felony
elements: Defendant restrained another person without consent
With purpose to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, facilitate commission of a felony, inflict physical injury, terrorize, or interfere with governmental function
notes: Kidnapping is always a Class Y Felony in Arkansas regardless of circumstances.

offense_class: Class A Felony (occupied structure); Class B Felony (unoccupied structure); Class C Felony (property over $500); Class D Felony (property under $500)
penalty_max: 30 years (Class A); 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant started a fire or caused an explosion
With purpose of destroying or damaging an occupiable structure or property of another
enhancements: Person injured or killed as a result
notes: Arkansas distinguishes arson severity based on whether the structure was occupied. Arson of an occupied structure is a Class A Felony.

statute_title: Attempted Murder in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Charged under the general attempt statute (§ 5-3-201) combined with the murder statute. Attempt reduces the offense by one class.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant caused serious physical injury to another person
By means of a deadly weapon
With the purpose of causing serious physical injury
notes: First-degree assault covers the use of a deadly weapon causing serious injury. Deadly weapon defined broadly in § 5-1-102.

offense_class: Class B Felony ($25,000+); Class C Felony ($5,000-$25,000); Class D Felony ($1,000-$5,000); Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over the property of another person
With the purpose of depriving the owner thereof
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (automatic Class B Felony)
notes: Thresholds: $25,000+ = Class B; $5,000-$25,000 = Class C; $1,000-$5,000 = Class D; under $1,000 = Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over property
Value exceeds $25,000
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Arkansas uses the 'theft of property' framework with value-based felony classes rather than 'grand theft' terminology.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over property
Value is under $1,000
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Under $1,000 threshold. Prior convictions can elevate the offense to a felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000); felony by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant concealed or took possession of merchandise
Of a retail establishment
With the purpose of depriving the merchant of the property without paying
notes: Arkansas has a specific shoplifting statute. Penalties generally follow the theft-by-value tier structure.

offense_class: Class B Felony (residential); Class C Felony (commercial)
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully
In a residential or commercial occupiable structure
With the purpose of committing any offense punishable by imprisonment
notes: Arkansas divides burglary into residential (§ 5-39-201, Class B Felony) and commercial (§ 5-39-201, Class C Felony). Both require entering with purpose to commit an offense.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully
In a residential occupiable structure of another person
With the purpose of committing any offense punishable by imprisonment
enhancements: Armed with a deadly weapon (aggravated residential burglary, § 5-39-204, Class Y Felony)
notes: Aggravated residential burglary involving a deadly weapon or physical injury is a Class Y Felony under § 5-39-204.

offense_class: Class C Felony or Class B Felony (depending on value)
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle
With the purpose of depriving the owner of the vehicle
notes: No separate motor vehicle theft statute. Charged as theft of property based on value. Most motor vehicles fall in the Class C or Class B felony range.

offense_class: Same class structure as theft based on value
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing or having good reason to believe the property was stolen
notes: Degree structure mirrors the theft statute based on value. Knowledge element can be established by circumstantial evidence.

statute_title: Criminal Mischief in the First Degree
offense_class: Class C Felony ($5,000+); Class D Felony ($1,000-$5,000); Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant purposely destroyed or damaged the property of another person
Without the consent of the owner
enhancements: Damage to a house of worship (enhanced penalties under § 5-71-215)
notes: Arkansas uses 'criminal mischief' rather than 'vandalism.' Degree based on damage amount. First degree is $5,000+ damage.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (dwelling); Class B Misdemeanor (building); Class C Misdemeanor (property)
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully
In or upon a dwelling, building, or property of another
Defendant knew entry or remaining was unlawful
notes: Trespass in a dwelling is the most serious (Class A Misdemeanor). Posted land trespass requires proper notice.

statute_title: Criminal Mischief in the First Degree
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant purposely destroyed or damaged property of another
Damage exceeds $5,000 in value
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Damage by means of explosive or fire
Damage to utility or communication property
notes: First degree requires over $5,000 damage. Second degree (§ 5-38-204) covers $1,000-$5,000 damage (Class D Felony). Third degree covers under $1,000 (Class A Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (third degree); Class C Felony (second degree); Class B Felony (first degree)
penalty_max: 1 year (third degree); 10 years (second degree); 20 years (first degree)
elements: Defendant purposely caused physical injury to a family or household member
Or recklessly caused physical injury with a deadly weapon
notes: Arkansas uses 'domestic battering' rather than 'domestic violence.' Family or household member includes spouses, former spouses, cohabitants, and parents of a common child.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant caused serious physical injury to a family or household member
With the purpose of causing serious physical injury
Or caused serious physical injury with a deadly weapon
notes: First-degree domestic battering is a Class B Felony. Third offense of third-degree domestic battering is elevated to a Class D Felony under § 5-26-305(c).

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Minor — First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant purposely created a substantial risk of death or serious physical injury
To a person less than 18 years of age
notes: First degree requires creating a substantial risk of death or serious physical injury. Second degree (§ 5-27-206) covers lesser risks.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly engaged in conduct creating a realistic threat of death, permanent disfigurement, or protracted impairment
To a child under 18
Or purposely caused serious physical injury
enhancements: Serious physical injury (Class B Felony under domestic battering statutes)
notes: May also be charged under domestic battering statutes if the relationship qualifies. Mandatory reporting requirements apply.

statute_title: Violation of an Order of Protection
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second within 5 years)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant willfully violated a condition of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 5 years (Class D Felony)
Violation involving physical contact or threat
notes: First violation is Class A Misdemeanor. Second within 5 years is a Class D Felony. May be arrested without a warrant.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second); Class C Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant purposely engaged in a course of conduct directed at another person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized or fear for their safety
The defendant knew or should have known the conduct was unwanted
notes: First offense is a Class A Misdemeanor. Escalates with subsequent offenses. Course of conduct requires a pattern of two or more acts.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant with purpose to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Struck, shoved, kicked, or otherwise touched another person
Or directed abusive, obscene, or threatening language toward another
In a manner likely to provoke a violent or disorderly response
notes: Separate provisions for cyberbullying and electronic harassment under § 5-71-217.

statute_title: Abuse of an Endangered or Impaired Person
offense_class: Class D Felony (abuse); Class B Felony (with serious physical injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly abused, neglected, or exploited an endangered or impaired person
Person is elderly (65+) or otherwise disabled
Defendant had a caretaker relationship
notes: Mandatory reporting under § 12-12-1708. Adult Protective Services investigates. Financial exploitation is a separate offense under § 5-28-103.

statute_title: Possession of Firearms by Certain Persons
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a convicted felon, adjudicated mentally ill, or committed involuntarily to a mental institution
notes: Arkansas is a permitless carry state as of 2023. Primary restriction is for prohibited persons. Class B Felony — notably harsh.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been previously convicted of a felony
notes: Applies to all persons convicted of a felony. Arkansas's permitless carry law does not change prohibitions for convicted felons.

statute_title: Carrying a Weapon in Prohibited Places
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (subsequent or in certain locations)
elements: Defendant carried a weapon
Into a location prohibited by law (school, courthouse, police station, etc.)
Or defendant was a prohibited person
notes: Arkansas adopted permitless carry. Most violations now relate to prohibited locations rather than lack of permit. Prohibited places listed in § 5-73-306.

statute_title: Unlawful Discharge of a Firearm from a Vehicle
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm from a vehicle
At or toward a person, occupied structure, or occupied vehicle
notes: Separate from reckless endangerment. Specifically targets drive-by shootings. Additional charges may apply for injury or death.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant obtained, recorded, or accessed another person's identifying information
Without authorization
With purpose to use the information to commit a crime
notes: Includes obtaining Social Security numbers, dates of birth, financial account information. Restitution is mandatory.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 6 years (Class D); 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over the property
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Embezzlement is a theory of theft, not a separate crime in Arkansas.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree); Class C Felony (second degree)
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With purpose to defraud
Instrument purports to be money, securities, postage stamps, revenue stamps, or instruments issued by government
notes: First-degree forgery covers government and financial instruments. Second-degree forgery (§ 5-37-202) covers deeds, wills, contracts, and other documents.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of Forged Instrument — First Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant possessed a forged instrument
Knowing it to be forged
With purpose to defraud by uttering or delivering it
notes: Counterfeiting of currency is primarily federal. State charges typically involve forged documents or instruments.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card or Debit Card / Hot Checks
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class D Felony ($1,000+)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); 6 years (Class D Felony)
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check, draft, or order for payment of money
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With purpose to defraud
notes: Hot Check Division of prosecuting attorney's office handles most cases. Defendant has 10 days after notice to make good on the check.

offense_class: Class D Felony (under $1,000); Class C Felony ($1,000-$25,000); Class B Felony ($25,000+)
penalty_max: 6 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C); 20 years (Class B)
elements: Defendant made a false statement or representation
In connection with an insurance claim or application
With purpose to defraud an insurer
notes: Includes filing false claims, staged accidents, and arson-for-profit. Mandatory restitution and potential civil penalties.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card or Debit Card
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class D Felony ($1,000+)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); 6 years (Class D Felony)
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or canceled
With purpose to defraud the card issuer or merchant
notes: Includes using a stolen card, forged card, or card obtained by fraud.

offense_class: Class B Felony
fine_max: $15,000 or twice the value of the property
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property represents proceeds of unlawful activity
With purpose to promote the unlawful activity or to conceal the source
notes: Arkansas enacted its money laundering statute under the Arkansas Criminal Code. Federal charges are also common.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
Created or confirmed a false impression of fact or law
Or failed to correct a false impression previously created
notes: General fraud is charged as theft by deception under the theft statute. Degree follows the standard value thresholds.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact with another person
By forcible compulsion
Or the victim was incapable of consent due to physical helplessness or mental incapacity
enhancements: Victim under 14 years of age (§ 5-14-124, first degree)
notes: Arkansas uses 'sexual assault' terminology. First-degree sexual assault (§ 5-14-124) involves victims under 14 and is a Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class Y Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse or deviate sexual activity with another person
By forcible compulsion
Or the victim was incapable of consent due to physical helplessness or mental disease or defect
Or victim was less than 14 years old
notes: Rape is a Class Y Felony — the most serious non-capital offense. Sex offender registration required. No statute of limitations for rape.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant exposed their sex organs in a public place
In a manner that would cause affront or alarm
Under circumstances in which the defendant knew the conduct was likely to be observed
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: First offense is Class A Misdemeanor. Subsequent offenses become a Class D Felony. Exposure to minors may result in sexual offense charges.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant engaged in or offered to engage in sexual activity
In exchange for money or other consideration
Or patronized a prostitute
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Both the person offering and the patron can be charged. Promoting prostitution (§ 5-70-104) is a separate felony. Human trafficking charges may also apply.

statute_title: Distributing, Possessing, or Viewing Sexual Material Depicting a Child
offense_class: Class C Felony (possession/viewing); Class B Felony (distribution); Class A Felony (production)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, distributed, or produced material depicting a child engaged in sexually explicit conduct
Defendant knew or had reason to know the subject was a minor
notes: Federal charges are common in addition to state charges. Sex offender registration required upon conviction.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration as required
notes: Must register within 3 business days. Arkansas Sex Offender Registration Act (§ 12-12-901 et seq.) requires registration for life for certain offenses.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact with another person
Victim was less than 14 years old
Defendant was 18 years or older
notes: Age of consent in Arkansas is 16. Sexual intercourse with a minor under 14 by a person 18+ is typically charged as rape (§ 5-14-103). Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant with purpose to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly creating a risk thereof
Engaged in fighting, violent, or tumultuous behavior
Or made unreasonable noise or obscene gestures in a public place
notes: Common add-on charge. Often paired with resisting arrest or public intoxication.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly resisted a person known to be a law enforcement officer
Effecting an arrest of the defendant or another person
enhancements: Use of physical force or violence (may upgrade charges)
notes: It is no defense that the arrest was unlawful if the officer was acting under color of authority. Physical resistance causing injury may lead to additional battery charges.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly obstructed, impaired, or hindered
The performance of a governmental function
By means of intimidation, force, violence, or physical interference or obstacle
notes: Broader than resisting arrest — covers interference with any governmental function.

offense_class: Varies (civil or criminal; summary or constructive)
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disruptive behavior in the courtroom
Or failed to appear as ordered
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive. Right to jury trial for serious criminal contempt.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance
To the degree that the defendant was likely to endanger themselves, others, or property
Or by being unreasonably annoying to people nearby
notes: Class C Misdemeanor. Can impact other pending cases and probation status.

offense_class: Class C Felony (felony case); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Required to appear at a specified time and place
Defendant purposely failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Class C Felony)
notes: Bench warrant issued upon failure to appear. Bond forfeiture in addition to criminal charges.

statute_title: Filing a False Report with Law Enforcement
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant reported false information to law enforcement
Knowing the information to be false
Regarding a crime or emergency
notes: Includes false reports of crimes and emergencies. Filing a false report that results in a SWAT response may carry additional charges.

statute_title: Terroristic Threatening in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant threatened to cause death or serious physical injury to another person
Or threatened to cause physical damage to a school or public building
With the purpose of terrorizing another person
notes: First degree covers threats to public buildings, schools, and mass casualties. Second degree (§ 5-13-301) covers individual threats.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant made a false sworn statement
In an official proceeding
The statement was material
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Perjury in an official proceeding is a Class C Felony. False swearing outside of official proceedings (§ 5-53-103) is a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
With the purpose of influencing the public servant's official action
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Receiving a bribe by a public servant (§ 5-52-104) is also a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree); Class C Felony (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree)
penalty_max: 20 years (first degree); 10 years (second degree); 1 year (third degree)
elements: Defendant escaped from custody
While charged with or convicted of a felony
From a correctional facility or while in the custody of a law enforcement officer
enhancements: Use of physical force or a deadly weapon (first degree)
notes: Three degrees. First degree involves use of force or a weapon. Second degree is escape from felony custody without force. Third degree is escape from misdemeanor custody.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (aggravated or second+)
elements: Defendant purposely or knowingly subjected an animal to cruel mistreatment
Or killed or injured an animal belonging to another without legal privilege or consent
enhancements: Aggravated cruelty to animals (§ 5-62-104, Class D Felony)
notes: First offense cruelty is Class A Misdemeanor. Aggravated cruelty (torture, mutilation) is Class D Felony. Animal fighting is a separate Class D Felony.

statute_title: Violation of Probation or Suspended Sentence
offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
penalty_max: Remaining suspended sentence on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation or given a suspended sentence
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was inexcusable
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Judge has discretion to revoke, modify, or continue probation. Defendant entitled to a revocation hearing. Standard of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Parole Board makes revocation decisions. Technical violations may result in graduated sanctions under Swift and Certain Sanctions program.

offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant aided, agreed to aid, or attempted to aid another person
In planning or committing an offense
With the purpose of promoting or facilitating the commission of the offense
notes: An accomplice is criminally liable to the same extent as the principal. A person who is legally incapable of committing an offense may be held as an accomplice.

offense_class: One class below the attempted offense (Class Y attempted = Class A attempt; etc.)
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the attempted offense
elements: Defendant purposely engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step
In a course of conduct intended to culminate in the commission of an offense
notes: Attempt reduces the offense classification by one level. Attempt to commit a Class Y Felony is a Class A Felony. Attempt to commit a Class A Misdemeanor is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in conduct that constitutes a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
With the purpose that the crime be committed
notes: Conspiracy classification is one level below the target offense. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is a defense if the defendant thwarted the success of the conspiracy.
